sources.fullCitation: ‘Le dernier déjeuner du “Canard aux Navets”.’ Comœdia (Paris), 15 March 1922, p. 2. Group photograph with a row-by-row caption naming Jean Legrand. Bibliothèque nationale de France / RetroNews.
sources.title: ‘Le Canard aux Navets’ luncheon group photograph
sources.creator: Photographer unidentified
sources.researchNote: The caption identifies the participants by row. Under ‘Tout en haut’, it lists J.-L. Croze, Boissyvon, Jean Legrand, Jean Pascal, René Hervil, Robert Saidreau and René Jeanne, placing Jean Legrand third from the left in the top row. The article text separately names ‘André et Jean Legrand’. In this early French-film context, Jean Legrand is Jean-René Legrand, Henri-André Legrand’s brother and collaborator. The media record preserves the complete group photograph and printed caption. Because the individual figure contains insufficient facial detail, it is not presented as Jean-René Legrand’s portrait; his person card therefore uses the standard monogram.

media.title: ‘Le Canard aux Navets’ luncheon group photograph, 1922
media.description: Group photograph from the ‘Canard aux Navets’ luncheon, published in Comœdia on 15 March 1922 together with a row-by-row caption. The caption includes ‘Jean Legrand’ as the third name under ‘Tout en haut’, and the accompanying report separately lists ‘André et Jean Legrand’ among the guests. The complete photograph and its printed caption are retained as documentary evidence; the individual figure is too small to serve as a reliable portrait.
media.altText: Halftone newspaper group photograph of guests at the ‘Canard aux Navets’ luncheon, followed by the original printed caption identifying participants by row.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph was published in France in 1922 without a photographer or agency credit and is treated as an anonymous work whose seventy-year French term expired at the end of 1992; publication before 1931 also places it in the public domain in the United States.
media.publicCaption: Guests at the ‘Canard aux Navets’ luncheon in Paris, 1922. The printed caption names Jean Legrand as the third person listed under ‘Tout en haut’; the full photograph is retained as documentary context rather than used as an individual portrait.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer unidentified; Comœdia, 15 March 1922, p. 2. RetroNews, Bibliothèque nationale de France.
